headline: Ocean-freight stress is HIGH and rising — 41.6/100; Strait of Hormuz is the lead driver, -88% vs normal

bullets.text: Global Ocean Freight Stress is **41.6/100** (**high**), up 1.5 pts week-over-week. 3 of 28 monitored chokepoints are disrupted.
The biggest driver is **Strait of Hormuz**, running **10.0/day** vs a normal of **80.4/day** (-88%) — a sustained level shift, not a fresh blip.
Tracking **9** active disruptions (timeline baseline established this run).
Also moving now: **Kerch Strait** is running **65% below** normal and **Mindoro Strait** is **57% above** normal (a diversion/reroute signal).
Market context: Brent crude **$92.9/bbl** (-2.54% intraday) — context for the energy-route chokepoints, not a stated cause.
Against the loaded sample trade book, **$134.5M** routes through disrupted lanes — an estimated **$401K** cost-of-delay ($211K–$645K).
